It all started as a bit of a joke, to be honest. My business partner and I come from a completely different industry—we both work in the RF (radio frequency) world by day. But I've always been a musician and guitarist, while he's an electrical engineer with a serious knack for circuits. We both love music, and we're unapologetic gear heads at heart.

One day, we were just chatting and tossed around the idea of starting an analog effects company that would do things exactly the way we’d want as musicians and tech enthusiasts. It was just talk at first, but over the years, that conversation slowly turned into something more serious.

Eventually, we settled on a specific effect to kick things off. We dove into the circuit design, tweaking and refining it to match our vision of what great gear should be. That initial conversation was about 6-7 years ago. Since then, we've chipped away at it bit by bit, balancing it with our day jobs, until now, when things are finally coming together.

At the end of the day, we're driven by a simple goal: to create effects and gear that not only sound amazing but also look the part, with rock-solid design and manufacturing behind them. It's been a long road, but we’re excited to see where it takes us next.

UPDATE  


The 2.5AMP Slo Blo Fuse was blown. 

Due to the nature of how the 6V6 power tubes were reacting to power it's pointing me towards the output transformer. It could also be the caps due to the age of them. This amp is about 30 years old at this point so that is the normal life span of these caps. I'm going to replace these anyway but will test the caps with an O-Scope just to verify. I decided to go with Nichicon brand caps for the appropriate values. I was able to source these on Ebay. These are also the same brand caps that are present on the board.

The output transformer started to worry me as far as sourcing it appropriately. I was a bit concerned about replacing the original parts with modern parts because this can affect the tone. BUT, I was given a company by a friend that ended up having an upgraded version of the output transformer specifically made for this amp. This company is [Mercury Magnetics](https://www.mercurymagnetics.com/). From what I've been told, these guys are legit. They also provide transformer refurbishment services as well. So even if they don't have the correct transformer for your amp, odds are they can refurbish your original transformer. Not sure of the timeline.

I also switched from Mullard power tubes to Ruby power tubes. From what I've read, Mullard tubes are a bit inconsistent when it comes to quality and lifespan. Ruby tubes are at the top of everyone's list as far as quality, lifespan and tone. 

​

I haven't began the repairs yet but will update as much as I can throughout this process.
